clue.text: Arsonist in boat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who lights fires
second meaning: a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships

explanation.surface: A fire-raiser hiding out aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are separate meanings joined by 'in'; the question mark flags the jokey reading of a fire-starter as a 'one who lights'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is literally one who sets things alight, and also a barge used in harbours to ferry cargo.

clue.text: Contributor to second row that's in a canal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in rugby, the ... are the players who form the second row of the scrum
second meaning: a gated section of a canal for raising boats

explanation.walkthrough: 'Second row' is a rugby term: the lock forwards form the second row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock is both a rugby forward position and an enclosed chamber on a waterway for changing water level.

clue.text: Jason's dog?

parts.note: Jason of Greek myth fetched back the Golden Fleece, so he was a fetcher of something golden

explanation.walkthrough: Jason and the Argonauts went to bring back the Golden Fleece; the dog breed's name, read literally, describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog breed's name, read literally, describes one who brings back a golden prize, as Jason did.

clue.text: Drive to spear fish in part of the Arctic

indicators.note: the fish is speared, so the other piece goes into it

parts.note: the tuna is a fish
DR is the street-name abbreviation for Drive

explanation.surface: An urge to harpoon fish somewhere in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the treeless, frozen plain found in Arctic regions.

clue.text: Repair broken sword

indicators.note: the word is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fixing a sword that has snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed thrusting blade.

clue.text: Sadly, one may be in its depths

definitions.text: Sadly, one may be in its depths

parts.words: Sadly, one may be in its depths
parts.note: the stock phrase 'in the depths of' this state describes someone utterly miserable

explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the idiom about being in the depths of utter hopelessness; 'Sadly' may tempt you to look for an anagram, but there is none.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'in the depths of' is classically completed by this word for complete loss of hope.

clue.text: Secure a point on the road to leave others behind

definitions.text: Secure a point on the road
definitions.meaning: first meaning: in football, a team playing away that earns one point has drawn away from home
second meaning: to pull ahead of rivals and open a gap

explanation.walkthrough: The road and point look like a map, but the first half is sports talk: a team on the road plays away, and a draw secures one point.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw away is to pull ahead and open up a gap on rivals in a race; a draw in an away game is also called this.

clue.text: At the weekend I get up burlesque

parts.note: SAT is the abbreviation for Saturday, part of the weekend
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Someone saying they get up for a comic show at the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: To burlesque something is to mock it through comic imitation, the same as lampooning it.

clue.text: Past caring for religion?

parts.note: 'past caring' sounds like indifference, but read literally it is caring for those of the past, as a faith

explanation.walkthrough: 'Past caring' looks like apathy toward religion; instead, read it as devotion to past generations, practised as a faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Venerating one's forebears is a religious practice found in many cultures, for example in China.

clue.text: Implacable, passed on loan with deductions

parts.note: to re-lend is to pass on what was itself on loan; re-lent
less means minus, with things deducted

explanation.surface: A grim lender sending on a loan after making cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read RELENT as re-lent: lent again, passed on as a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone implacable cannot be appeased and never lets up or softens.

clue.text: Mark firm losing half of capital

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the capital city's name drops its back half, so only the front half is kept

parts.note: London is the UK capital

explanation.surface: A company shedding half its value in the capital leaves a mark on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' suggests a stain or grade, but it is a punctuation mark; the capital is London.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation symbol, one of the marks used in writing.

clue.text: Exam is a sort of joke

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... test, as in science or driving
second meaning: a ... joke is a prank played on someone

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a student's grumble about a test; the two parts are separate meanings joined by 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on assessment is called a practical, and a prank is a practical joke.

clue.text: Two men in a boat, working: one was a guitarist

parts.note: George and Harris are two of the three men in Jerome K Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Two boatmen hard at work, one of whom used to play guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Men in a Boat is an 1889 comic novel about J, George and Harris rowing up the Thames; two of them supply most of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Harrison was the lead guitarist of the Beatles.

clue.text: To replace relic, snoop in cemetery

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a different place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone poking about a graveyard to swap one relic for another.
explanation.definitionFit: A necropolis is a large ancient burial ground, literally a 'city of the dead'.

clue.text: Corny stuff for listeners

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... of corn are the grain-bearing heads of the plant
second meaning: the organs we hear with

explanation.walkthrough: 'Corny' suggests trite jokes, but here it literally means made of corn; 'for' just joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal heads are called ears, and ears are also the organs of hearing.

clue.text: A local perch?

parts.note: a local is a British pub, and a perch is a high seat; the tall seat at a pub counter

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub; 'perch' suggests a fish or bird, but it is a high seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall seat at a pub counter is where drinkers sit, a fitting raised roost.

clue.text: Come across a drunkard, upside down and unconscious

indicators.note: the first word stretches across the others, holding them inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

explanation.surface: Finding a drunk flat out and out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come across' reads as 'meet', but here 'across' tells you the word Come spans the rest; 'upside down' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A comatose person is in a coma, deeply insensible and beyond waking.

clue.text: In pond leaves large mixed display

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big jumbled show of foliage in a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: The broad floating leaves of water lilies rest on the surface of ponds.

clue.text: Consciously old-fashioned, suitable to modernise later

parts.note: retro describes a deliberately revived older style
fit means suitable, as in fit for purpose

explanation.surface: Something deliberately vintage that is fine to update further down the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrofit is to add new components or features to an existing older building or machine.

clue.text: Said to employ females

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word for employ sounds like the answer

parts.note: to employ something is to use it

explanation.definitionFit: Ewes are female sheep, so the plural noun names females of that animal.

clue.text: Not placed in a quarter?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in racing, only the first three are placed, so the next finisher misses out
second meaning: one of four equal parts

explanation.walkthrough: In horse racing a 'placed' finish is in the top three, so the next position is just out of the places.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal after third misses the places in a race, and as a fraction it equals one part in four.

clue.text: What Humphrey hung in the loo?

definitions.text: What Humphrey hung in the loo?

parts.words: What Humphrey hung in the loo?
parts.note: a slang word for a toilet followed by a word for pictures spells the film star Humphrey's surname

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog' is British slang for toilet; pictures hung there are bog art, which is the surname of the film star Humphrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was the Hollywood star of Casablanca, and his surname splits into toilet plus pictures.

clue.text: School flag: red, green and blue, say

parts.note: a primary is a primary school
a regiment's or ship's flag is its colours

explanation.surface: A school banner coloured red, green and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Red, green and blue are the additive primaries of light, which is why 'say' marks them as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Red, green and blue are the basic hues from which light of other shades is mixed.

clue.text: Highlander, perhaps heading away from the racecourse

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, goes away from the word

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a royal racecourse in England; removing its first letter leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highlander lives in the Scottish Highlands, so is one example of a person from Scotland.

clue.text: Survive without food, broadcasting in real time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to subsist on nothing

explanation.walkthrough: The comma separates two meanings: a hyperbole for going without food, and a broadcaster's term for transmitting live.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone said to subsist on nothing 'lives on air', while a programme going out as it happens is live on air.

clue.text: For the occasion, speaker's to take more white wine

indicators.note: what a speaker says, spoken out loud, gives the sound of the words

parts.note: to add is to take more, and hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A speaker announces they will have another glass of white.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is the traditional British name for Rhine white wine; ADD HOCK spoken sounds like the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin for something arranged for a particular purpose or situation only.

clue.text: Ways one may be so far ahead?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: roads in a town

definitions.text: one may be so far ahead
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to be '... ahead' is to be far in front

explanation.walkthrough: The second part completes the British idiom 'streets ahead', meaning much better or far in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets are roads, routes or thoroughfares, and the plural also forms the idiom for a big lead.

clue.text: Pot shot taken wildly in a potentially dangerous area

indicators.note: the letters are handled in a wild, random way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A random shot fired in a risky zone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspot is a place of trouble or conflict, such as a region where fighting may break out.
